## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

# T-088  A writer's refusal is kept, and every refusal a batch met is disposed

_One task, one pull request. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. Source: the owner's five statements of 2026-11-13 on what the pipeline cannot execute (`grep -n -F 'Owner statements 2026-11-13 (eleventh set)' references/project-standards.md`, statements 1 to 5), the adjudication's Q10 and proposal P6 (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/ADJUDICATION.md`). Every number in this file was read on 2026-11-13 on commit `66a5ba8a` and is given with the command that produces it: re-run the command; do not trust the number._

**Pilot status.** Not piloted. Authored 2026-11-13 by the fold of the Edmonton case study. Expect to find a defect in this file, and report it rather than work around it.

## 1. Identity

| | |
|---|---|

## 2. Preconditions

- **The integration base.** `origin/main` once the workplan's pull request is merged, otherwise the remote branch carrying the newest commit to this folder (the set-up block's first line finds it).
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** none.
- **Owner decisions:** none. The register reading of the owner's first statement is the one the rules support (ADJUDICATION Q10: rules 3 and 10 and CLAUDE.md §4 leave two lawful acts when a writer refuses, write through an existing verb or park). The other reading, an agent writing the canonical row by hand, is the open owner question OD-54 (the adjudication's AQ-8), and **nothing in this task builds it**: so OD-54 holds no part of this task.
- **Tests that must be red before you start:** `T088-01` (section 6): a refused call leaves no line anywhere.
- **Set-up.**

```
cd /home/user/guidebook
bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh && python3 -c "import pydantic, jsonschema, yaml"
git fetch origin
W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1); echo "BASE=$BASE"
git switch -c task/t-088-refusal-capture-and-disposition "$BASE"         # real execution only
sha256sum data/guidebook.db                                  # record it; this task has no migration
export SCRATCH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guidebook-t-088" && mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/t.db"
```
- Shell variables do not survive between tool calls: begin every later block with the `W=…; BASE=…` and `export SCRATCH=…` lines. **Real execution:** `/session-open` first. **Pilot:** no `/session-open`, stay on the given branch, stop after section 7.

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

When a writer refuses, the sentence that says why is the only record of what the batch tried to hold and could not. It is printed once and lost: the session's command log keeps the command and a hash of what was printed, not the words, and its exit code is not reliable. So a determination can omit a figure, or an inadequacy statement, that its source held, and nothing shows that the batch met it and what became of it. The owner asked for a register of what the pipeline cannot execute, "so we aren't losing content" and "that way we aren't held up" (statements 1 and 2).

**Evidence commands** (read-only):

```
python3 -c "import json;print(sorted(json.loads(open('scratchpad/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/commands.jsonl').readline())))"
grep -n 'MEASURED CORRECTION' .claude/hooks/record-command.py
grep -n 'except Refusal as exc' scripts/db.py scripts/assess/assess_cell.py
grep -n '^class Refusal' scripts/dbcore.py scripts/assess/assess_cell.py
git grep -n -F 'refusals.jsonl' -- scripts .claude skills governance | head -3
```

**Output on 2026-11-13:** the log's keys are `bytes, command, cwd, exit, interrupted, is_error, response_keys, session_id, stderr_bytes, stderr_sha256, stdout_sha256, tool, ts` (no output text); the hook's own comment records that `exit` is not reliable; one catch point in each of `scripts/db.py` and `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`, each `sys.exit(f"REFUSING: {exc}")`; two `Refusal` classes (`scripts/dbcore.py` and the engine's own, kept apart on purpose: read the engine's class docstring); no `refusals.jsonl` anywhere. If a capture already exists, the defect is fixed: stop (section 9).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect. **Do nothing** fails: the sentence is gone and the retry history with it. **A convention alone** (list what you met in `/batch-done`) fails the same way: the operator cannot list a sentence nobody kept. **Reuse:** the register of what is owed is the `gaps` table (`add-gap`; T-013's typed subject columns); the replay command is the refused argv itself, so no payload column or table is added. **Smallest code:** the capture, and one small reader of one session.

1. **Capture, one home: `dbcore.record_refusal(script, argv, sentence)`.** Called at the two catch points, before `sys.exit`: in `scripts/db.py`, `dbcore.record_refusal("scripts/db.py", sys.argv[1:], str(exc))`; in `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` the same with `"scripts/assess/assess_cell.py"` (the engine already imports `dbcore`: `grep -n '^import dbcore' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`). The function, stdlib only like the rest of `dbcore`:
   - reads the session stem from `REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad/CURRENT"`; returns, writing nothing, when that file is missing, or `REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad" / <stem>` is not a directory (CLAUDE.md §7: the folder must be named identically to `CURRENT`'s content);
   - reads the value after `--session` in `argv` (bare, with a trailing `.md` removed); returns, writing nothing, unless it equals the stem;
   - appends one JSON line to `scratchpad/<stem>/refusals.jsonl`: `ts` (`dbcore.now()`), `session`, `script`, `verb` (`argv[0]` for `scripts/db.py`; the script's own name for the engine), `argv`, `sentence`, and `db` (`str(dbcore.db_path())`, or the engine's `--db` value: which database refused);
   - never raises: an `OSError` writing the line is swallowed, so the refusal's exit and message are unchanged.
   **Chosen (authoring 2026-11-13): capture only a call whose `--session` is the running session.** Rejected: capture every refusal (the tests call `db.py` as a subprocess and refuse on purpose under `--session session_fixture` and the like, `grep -n 'def cli' -A3 scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py`; their refusals would fill the running session's record with fixtures); an environment switch to turn capture off (every test and probe must remember it, and one that forgets floods the record). A probe run under `session_probe` is deliberately not captured: it is not the batch's content.
   **Chosen: the line holds only what was said and done.** The derived fields (the stage the verb writes to, the tables it touches, the rule ids the sentence cites, a signature that clusters recurring refusals) are computed by the reader, T-089, from these fields and the live repository. Rejected: storing them in the line, as first proposed. `dbcore` is stdlib only and cannot read `governance/stage-map.yaml`; and a derived value stored beside its input drifts when the derivation improves (rule 5, rule 8): a signature normalised one way in October and another in December splits one class in two.
2. **A reader of one session, and the disposition: `scripts/audit/refusal_register.py`.** Stdlib only. Two subcommands:
   - `list [--session S]` (default: `scratchpad/CURRENT`): reads `scratchpad/<S>/refusals.jsonl` and prints, per refusal, its `ts`, `verb`, the sentence's first 160 characters and its disposition or `UNDISPOSED`; then `EXAMINED: <n> refusal(s)`; exits 1 when any is undisposed, 0 otherwise (also 0 with `EXAMINED: 0` when the file does not exist: say "no refusal captured").
   - `dispose --session S --ts T --as retried|parked|waived [--gap-id G] [--reason R]`: appends a line `{"kind": "disposition", "refusal_ts": T, "as": ..., "gap_id": ..., "reason": ..., "ts": now}` to the same file. Refuses (`REFUSING:` and exit 1): a `T` no refusal line of the file carries; `parked` without `--gap-id`, or with a gap id absent from the `gaps` table of the database the refusal line names (`db`), or, if that file is gone, of `data/guidebook.db`; `waived` without `--reason`; a second disposition of the same refusal.
   **Chosen:** the three dispositions are declared once, as a constant in this script, and read from there by `list` and `dispose` (the owner's 2026-11-12 line: a rule declared once in a stated place is not hard-coding, `grep -n -F "isn't hardcoding necessarily" references/project-standards.md`). Rejected: a table with a CHECK (a disposition is a fact about a session's record, held beside it in the committed scratchpad, rule 6; no other table reads it).
3. **The Layer 0 rule, in `/batch-done`.** In `.claude/commands/batch-done.md`, after the three gate lines, add:
   ```
   python3 scripts/audit/refusal_register.py list --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
   ```
   and the sentence: "Every writer refusal this batch met is disposed before the batch is done: **retried** (the writer was right; the corrected call succeeded), **parked** (its content waits: file a gap with `db.py add-gap`, typed by its subject, and keep the refused argv, which is the replay command), or **waived** (with a reason). An undisposed refusal is a batch that is not done."
4. **The Layer 2 protocol, in the skill.** In `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`, section "Resume and exceptions", add one paragraph: "**When a writer refuses** (Layer 2 protocol; the capture is Layer 1, the `/batch-done` rule Layer 0): acknowledge (correct the call and write the row, if the refusal was right), or refuse-and-park (keep the refused argv, file a gap naming what is held back, and go on: the batch is not held up), then replay (the parked content is written through the sanctioned writer in a later research pull request, after the tooling pull request that closes the gap has merged, rule 10). Never write the row by hand: the content waits in the register, not in the database (`CLAUDE.md` rules 3 and 10; OD-54 is open). `refusal_register.py list` shows what the batch met."
5. **Not built here:** the reader across sessions, its classes and its cues (T-089); a registered check (review is the gate until it proves insufficient: ADJUDICATION Q10's Layer 0 note); any path that writes a canonical row by hand (OD-54).

**What reads what this task adds:** `/batch-done` (the `list` line); the research batch's pull request (the disposition list); T-089 (every committed `refusals.jsonl`). **What wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it:** a determination that omits a figure or an inadequacy statement its source held, with no record that it was met. **What it makes deletable:** nothing.

**Code size.** Report `git diff --shortstat "$(git merge-base HEAD "$BASE")" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` after `git add`, and name what reads each addition.

### 4a. Design: the refusal register (owner statements 1 to 5, 2026-11-13)

*This subsection is the design both T-088 and T-089 build to. It decides no doctrine.*

- **Layers** (CLAUDE.md §3). **Layer 1, the carrier:** `dbcore.record_refusal`, one home for every writer, and the line's shape. **Layer 2, per-stage triage:** each stage meets the refusals its writers make, and the protocol is the same at every stage: *acknowledge* (the row is written), *refuse-and-park* (the sentence and argv are kept, a gap is filed, the batch goes on), *replay* (through the sanctioned writer, in a research pull request after the tooling merges). Which checks and which skill section a refusal at a stage cues is derived by T-089, not listed. **Layer 0, the gate:** `/batch-done`'s rule that every refusal met is disposed; a registered check only if review proves insufficient. **Layer 3:** the parked content and the rows the replay writes. This is a Layer 2 protocol on a Layer 1 carrier under a Layer 0 gate, not a new stage-pair contract: the stage-pair checks (`judgment_handoff_shape`, `derivation_handshake_integrity`) test rows already written, and a refusal happens at a writer, inside a stage.
- **The five failure classes** (the adjudication's; recorded on the disposition and the gap, never as a second vocabulary). (1) *A policy refusal that was right:* disposition `retried`, no gap. (2) *A missing verb or field:* `parked`; a gap, category `SW` (the category the register already uses for writer gaps: `select category, count(*) from gaps group by 1`), replayed after the tooling pull request. (3) *A tool defect:* `parked`; a gap, category `SW`. (4) *An environment block* (a publisher 403, a lost connection): not a writer refusal, so it is not captured here; its homes exist (`--processing-blocked-reason`, and the deferred acts of T-079). (5) *A data conflict:* the writers already accept a contest row or a follow-up, so it is `retried` through those verbs, or `waived` with the reason. Classes (2) and (3) share `SW`; the gap's description says which. **Chosen:** no new gap category. Rejected: a failure-class column (the owner asked that refusals be "dynamically typed/categorized", statement 4; T-089 derives the class of a refusal from its sentence's signature and its disposition, and a typed column would be a second, curated vocabulary).
- **The replay rule.** Parked content is replayed through the sanctioned writer in a research pull request after the tooling that closes its gap has merged (rule 10). The refused argv is the replay command; the replay session runs it as written, or as the closing tooling's new verb requires, and closes the gap.
- **The line the owner's first statement leaves open.** "alongside having an agent fix it by hand with correct context" is read as: the agent records the intended row (the argv), its refusal and a proposed amendment in the register. A canonical row written by hand is **not** part of T-088 or T-089; it is OD-54 (the adjudication's AQ-8), open.
- **The cue** (statement 5: "a cue to run a script/double check a protocol or skill/etc to ensure that the digest was actually performed correctly"): T-089 prints, for each refusal a batch met, the registered checks and the skill section of the refused verb's stage, derived from the repository; `/batch-done` re-runs those checks and re-reads that section before the batch is called done.

## 5. Caller sweep

Names to sweep: `except Refusal as exc`, `REFUSING:`, `record_refusal`, `batch-done`.

**What a caller is.** A hit is a *caller* when its behaviour or its truth changes with this task: a test that asserts a refusal's stderr or exit (the capture must leave both unchanged: such a test going red has found a changed exit); a skill or command sentence that says how a refusal is handled, or that a refusal leaves no record; a registry entry. A mention stays true. Fixing a caller is in scope (CLAUDE.md rule 4). Left out: `workplan/` except `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/machines.yaml`, `references/project-standards.md`, `scripts/migrations/`, `sessions/`, `_archived/`, `audits/`, `versions/`, `transcripts/`, `scratchpad/`.

```
N='<name>'
git grep -n -F -e "$N" -- scripts schemas .github .claude skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'
python3 -c "import yaml,sys;print([c['id'] for c in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if sys.argv[1] in str(c)])" "$N"
git grep -n -F -e "$N" -- governance architecture CLAUDE.md references workplan/pipeline-state-graph/machines.yaml ':(exclude)references/project-standards.md' ':(exclude)references/search-log'
```

## 6. Verification

**Step 1, before any edit: the before-run.**
```
CHECKS="test_run_pipeline_refusals test_db_amend_writers test_assess_cell_pilot claude_skills_loadable skill_vocabulary_audit"
for c in $CHECKS; do cmd=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys,shlex;print(shlex.join(next(x['cmd'] for x in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if x['id']==sys.argv[1])))" $c); $cmd > "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" 2>&1; echo "$c rc=$? | $(grep -E '^ *EXAMINED:|RESULTS|FAILED|VERDICT' "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-200)"; done
```
Record what is red before (`skill_vocabulary_audit` was red on 2026-11-12) and carry on.

**Step 2: red before, green after** (cases `T088-01`… in `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py`; prefix free: `git grep -c 'T088-' scripts/tests/`). The tests never touch the real `scratchpad/CURRENT`: they call `dbcore.record_refusal` in-process with `dbcore.REPO_ROOT` pointed at a temporary directory that holds its own `scratchpad/CURRENT` and session folder (patch the module attribute for the call and restore it).
- `T088-01` a refusal whose argv carries `--session <the temp stem>` appends exactly one line with the six fields and `db`; red before (no function: assert the attribute exists, so an absent function cannot pass).
- `T088-02` a refusal under another session, with no `--session`, with `CURRENT` missing, and with the folder named differently from `CURRENT`, appends nothing.
- `T088-03` an unwritable session folder (`chmod` it read-only on the temp tree): the function returns without raising.
- `T088-04` through the CLI: `db.py` refused under `--session session_fixture` (choose the refusal by an existing case of the file) exits 1 with the same `REFUSING:` text as before, and the real session folder's `refusals.jsonl` (if any) does not change size.
- `T088-05` `refusal_register.py`: on the temp tree, `list` exits 1 with one `UNDISPOSED`; `dispose --as parked` without `--gap-id` refuses, with a gap id that is not a row refuses (the id built by query to be absent), with a real gap id (built on a scratch copy by `add-gap`, labelled `TASK-FIXTURE`) succeeds; `list` then exits 0; a second `dispose` of the same refusal refuses.
- Seeded defect: drop the session-equality test in `record_refusal`; `T088-02` goes red; restore.

**Fixtures** go to a copy or a temporary tree, are labelled `TASK-FIXTURE`, and never reach `data/guidebook.db` or the real scratchpad.

**Step 3: after-run.** The same loop with `after-`; compare failing lines check by check; nothing new may fail; `test_run_pipeline_refusals`'s `EXAMINED:` grows only by the T088 cases.

**Step 4: the gate, once.**
```
W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1)
scripts/preflight.sh --base "$BASE" --explain > "$SCRATCH/gate.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E '^(RESULT|PREFLIGHT|SELFTEST)|FAIL|NOTHING-IN-SCOPE' "$SCRATCH/gate.txt"
```
Run once, in the background. If T-075 is not yet merged, run `python3 scripts/audit/research_tooling_separation.py --base "$BASE"` by hand and report it. `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` must not move.

## 7. Commit

```
git add -A . ':!transcripts' ':!*commands.jsonl'
git commit -m "governance: keep each writer refusal and dispose of every refusal a batch met [$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')]" -m "<body: the owner's statements it answers; evidence before and after; the capture rule and why; callers; checks with EXAMINED>" -m "<the attribution trailers your own session instructions give>"
```

## 8. What you must NOT do

- Do not change a refusal's text, its exit code or what it writes (nothing).
- Do not capture output other than the refusal sentence; do not capture a call whose `--session` is not the running session.
- Do not add a gap category, a table or a column; do not register a check.
- Do not build any path that writes a canonical row by hand (OD-54).
- Do not write `data/guidebook.db`. Do not run `run_checks.py --all`, `bootstrap.sh` or `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Do not push to `main`, rebase or force-push; do not subscribe to pull-request activity.

## 9. Stop conditions

Stop and report when: a capture of refusal sentences already exists; a refusal's exit or message changes; a test that refuses on purpose writes a line into the real session folder; the engine cannot import `dbcore` (its import roster changed); a check green before is red after; `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` changes.

## 10. Rollback

Before merge: close the pull request, delete the branch. After merge: `git revert <merge commit>` in a new pull request; the captured lines in committed scratchpads stay as records.

## 11. Adversarial pass and pull request

Real execution only. `/adversarial` once; `/batch-done`; push; open the pull request last, once, against the integration base; call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it immediately; push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change, never `[skip ci]` on the final push.

# Batch 1: what was executed, what stopped, and what later tasks must read

_Written at the end of the batch (owner instruction 2026-11-15, "sweep … forward and backward"). Derive every count from `git log`; none is typed here. The line-by-line account of what the critics found and what is still the owner's is `scratchpad/session_2026-11-15-remediation-stack/sweep-list.md`._

## Later tasks: read these before executing

- **T-056** adds a third successor column "and widens this CHECK": the check on `base_taxonomy_identity` is a column-level CHECK carried by `superseded_by_identity` (migration 135, added in place). Widening it needs a table rebuild (as 133/136 did), not an ALTER.

from contextlib import contextmanager

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refusal — the exception a writer raises when it will not do the thing asked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Refusal(ValueError):
    """A deliberate refusal by a writer, addressed to the operator.

    THE REFUSALS ARE THE PRODUCT. CLAUDE.md §4: "`db.py` refuses, and that is its whole
    value. A writer that merely INSERTs is worse than hand SQL because it looks safe."
    Those refusals cite rulings, name the remedy and say `Nothing was written` — and
    until 2026-09-10 every one of them arrived at the terminal as the last line of a
    Python traceback, with the part the operator needs at the bottom of a stack they did
    not ask for. A `db.py`/`dbcore` refusal is now printed as a sentence.

    A SUBCLASS RATHER THAN A BARE `except ValueError`, and the distinction is
    load-bearing. `ValueError` is also what `int('abc')` raises, what a mis-typed
    conversion raises, and what pydantic's `ValidationError` IS. Those are DEFECTS, not
    refusals, and a defect's traceback is the evidence of where it lives. Catching the
    base class would print them as one-line refusals and teach their reader to retry the
    command instead of reading the bug. So: raise `Refusal` where the writer is saying
    no on purpose; leave everything else alone, and let it keep its stack.

    `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` carries its own class of the same name for the same
    reason. It is a deliberate second definition, not an oversight: that engine's import
    roster is documented per PILOT-MANIFEST.md §4 and imports only `schemas.*`, and
    coupling a determination engine to the write library to share an exception class
    would buy nothing either surface can use — neither ever catches the other's.
    """


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths — one resolution each, and no other module should compute these.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def is_tracked(rel_path: str) -> bool:
    """True iff `rel_path` (repo-relative) is in the git index (staged counts, committed or not).

    An untracked transcript is not an artefact (CLAUDE.md rule 6): its entire contents live in
    ephemeral container storage until committed, so a session could name a file that a later
    clone will never see. The one home of the test; `db.py` and `retrieval_log.py` call it.
    """
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(REPO_ROOT), "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", rel_path],
        capture_output=True)
    return result.returncode == 0


def db_path() -> Path:
    """The database this process should use.

    Resolved at CALL time, not import time. The research runbook points
    GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH at a scratch copy inline on every invocation because the
    harness resets env between shells; a module-level constant captured at import
    would silently ignore that and write the canonical file.
    """
    return Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", str(REPO_ROOT / "data" / "guidebook.db")))

---
description: The gate that decides whether a research batch is actually finished
---

Never claim a batch is done from your own reading of it. Run the gate the
SessionStart contract names:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/search_log_completeness.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
```

The second line is RC4 (advisory): it FAILs if this session wrote to any of the 2026-08-19
RULE's research tables and no closed adversarial pass names it. That FAIL is not a reason to
close pass 1; LED-192 holds it open (`/adversarial` step 3). Run it on `CURRENT`, not via
`run_checks.py --all --battery research` — that battery's other session-scoped checks
(`research_dod_session`, `author_fidelity`, `citation_mining_session`) are still pointed
at `LATEST-RESEARCH`, which names the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of this one.

The third line is I5, also on `CURRENT`: it reads the WebSearch/WebFetch ledger the
harness hook wrote and FAILs a WebSearch query that no `search_executions.query_text` of
this session contains — a search you ran and did not log (R8). Log it with
`db.py log-search --backfill 1`: the row is a reconstruction, not a log made as the search
ran, and the `--prior-expectation` it still requires is written after the results, so it
is post hoc and must say so. Its REPORTED lines (unpersisted WebFetch URLs, bare curl/wget
hosts, and web rows logged with no web line on the ledger — a hook that may not have
fired) belong in the session record; they do not fail, and a NOTHING-IN-SCOPE verdict does
not clear them. It witnesses WebSearch and WebFetch only: a search run through an MCP tool
(Consensus, PubMed, Scholar Gateway) leaves no line, so a PASS says nothing about those. R8 still
owes each of them a `log-search` row, and `record_file` its result (DR-2026-09-26 §2.2b); the
gate can check neither.

**The session id is the bare stem in the DB and carries `.md` in pointer files.**
Wrong form scopes the gate to zero rows and every rule reports PASS over an empty
subject — green, and meaningless.

If it fails, the batch is not done. Fix the rows, re-emit, re-run. Do not
baseline the failure away: `governance/research-contract-baseline.json` ratchets
DOWN only, and raising a count there forgives fresh violations invisibly.

When it passes, confirm the corpus posture has not regressed:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --all
```

Then commit the scratchpad and the agent transcripts (`scripts/preserve_transcripts.py`)
— a read-only subagent writes nothing at all, so its entire workings live in
ephemeral container storage until they are copied out.

A batch can read a document whose provisions are for blind, Deaf, cognitive and fatigue-limited people and still
write only mobility figures, because those are the quantities the catalogue holds. Print what the catalogue can
and cannot speak about, read-only, against the database the batch used (`GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH`, else

               "that has been run against is no longer pristine, and a re-run for the "
               "same cell is refused by the row-identity index; and comparing two runs "
               "for determinism means two fresh copies, not one DB run twice. The "
               "canonical DB is refused outright.")
    ap.add_argument("--db", required=True,
                    help="scratch DB, READ for the evidence and WRITTEN with the "
                         "determination (NEVER data/guidebook.db)")
    ap.add_argument("--emit-sql", required=True,
                    help="path for the replayable SQL copy of the rows this run also "
                         "commits into --db")
    ap.add_argument("--parameter-id", dest="parameter_id", type=int, required=True,
                    help="base_parameters.parameter_id — THE SUBJECT (owner 2026-08-26)")

    # topic the determination is being RECORDED under: it lands in the report and in
    # the gap description's context, and it is required so a determination cannot be
    # made without saying which piece of work it belongs to.
    ap.add_argument("--slug", required=True,
                    help="the topic this determination is recorded under. It does NOT "
                         "select evidence -- sources are gathered by the extractions "
                         "they hold for --parameter-id whose live lens links carry every "
                         "lens code the cell states.")
    ap.add_argument("--identity", help="base_taxonomy_identity.identity_code")
    ap.add_argument("--icf", help="base_icf.icf_code — a real ICF b/d code")
    ap.add_argument("--needs", help="access_needs.need_code")

    # that the replay would refuse — the scratch state and the report both looked clean
    # and only the migration caught it. An engine whose own run is laxer than the replay
    # tells you the wrong thing at the moment you are deciding whether to replay.
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")

        "-- determination — generated by scripts/assess/assess_cell.py",

        "-- Replay onto the canonical DB through emit_data_migration.py -> migrate_db.py,",

        "-- before replay — a stale copy can collide with gap ids created since.",

        "-- (DR-2026-08-19 §12.0 F5/F6), so the wrapper was never load-bearing — but a",

        "-- and emit_data_migration.py says bodies are never wrapped. Relying on the",

    base = max(

        conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(convergence_id), 0) FROM convergence_assessment").fetchone()[0])
    conv_id = base

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refusal helpers — the CLI's value is that it REFUSES, and a refusal is only
# trustworthy if its vocabulary is the live one.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def columns(conn, table: str) -> list:
    """The table's real column names, read from the live schema."""
    return [r[1] for r in conn.execute('PRAGMA table_info("%s")' % table)]


def stamp_for(conn, table: str, session: str) -> dict:
    """Audit columns THIS table actually has, filled in.

    NOT every table carries created_at/created_by_session. `source_locators` carries
    NEITHER -- it is a pre-reset stash whose rows predate the audit convention. A
    writer that assumes the stamp is universal fails at INSERT with "table X has no
    column named created_at", which is how this function came to exist: the Act-2
    rehearsal refused all 8 writes for exactly that reason, and the refusal was mine,
    not the data's.

    Derive from the schema; never assume the convention holds.
    """
    have = set(columns(conn, table))
    return {k: v for k, v in audit(session).items() if k in have}


def exists(conn, table: str, column: str, value) -> bool:
    """Is `value` a live key in table.column? The FK check a CLI does before writing."""

"""scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py — the pass exists for what this session wrote.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Three canonical statements already require an adversarial pass on every
research/synthesis diff (the 2026-08-19 RULE; DR-2026-09-11 clause 2; pipeline-contract.yaml's
cross_stage/definition-of-done), and none of the three had a committed enforcer.
`claims_docket.py` scans for claim-words in prose; the word "adversarial" appears in its
comments only. Batch 20's own antagonist pass ran the SAME model as its author while its
record called it independent, and nothing caught that because nothing recorded a pass in
checkable form (DR-2026-09-26-recurring-defect-shapes-remediation.md, RC4).

THE SUBJECT TABLES are not a list in this file (CLAUDE.md rule 8). They are parsed from the
2026-08-19 RULE's own text in references/project-standards.md, anchored on a quote that must
occur exactly once. If the ruling's wording ever moves, this audit exits 2 ("cannot run")
rather than silently examining nothing.

THE COLUMNS are every column of those tables whose name ENDS in `_by_session` (a substring
match would wrongly catch bpc_metadata.supersession_check_complete). `connection_targets` is
NOT one of the RULE's limb-(a) tables and this script never touches it; it is named here only
because it is DR-2026-09-26 section 1.2's own example of why OQ-8's wider scope (every
writable table, not just the RULE's list) needs a separate design -- that table has no
`_by_session` column at all, so a widened version of this script would have to decide what
"this session wrote to it" even means there. This script's own subject, derived below, never
includes it.

SCOPE IS THE RULE'S LIST, DELIBERATELY, until the owner answers OQ-8 (widen to every writable
table). Widening this file ahead of that answer would implement OQ-8 while the DR text says
it is still open.

`CURRENT`, not `LATEST-RESEARCH`: the latter names the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of
the current one (CLAUDE.md section 7), so a mid-session check against it silently audits
someone else's batch. Accepts either spelling (bare stem or `<stem>.md`) when matching rows,
because CURRENT holds the bare form today but has not always (batches 11-15 wrote branch

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/readonly_db_open_audit.py — a script that only reads must open read-only.

WHY THIS EXISTS
---------------
Opening the canonical database read-write to read it has two costs, and the
second is the dangerous one.

1. SQLite creates `-wal` and `-shm` sidecars next to `data/guidebook.db` on a
   read-write open, and may checkpoint on close. The repo's `.gitignore` already
   carries an entry for these, which is evidence the mechanism is live rather
   than theoretical.
2. **A read-write handle is a write the reproducibility gate cannot see.** The
   blocking `migration_reproducibility` check compares `PRAGMA user_version` plus
   `COUNT(*)` on six tables (CLAUDE.md §0 rule 4). A checkpoint, a stray UPDATE,
   or an accidental commit of a mutated binary changes none of those counts. The
   migrations-only rule is absolute; its detection floor is not. Every read-write
   handle held by something that never intends to write is an unnecessary way for
   the canonical DB to change without a migration.

Measured 2026-08-06 before the sweep this check was written for: 43 non-legacy
scripts opened the DB, and only 16 of them read-only.

SCOPE — a script is IN SCOPE when all three hold
   1. it is not under a one-time/legacy directory (EXCLUDE_PARTS, mirroring
      db_path_env_audit.py so "legacy" means one thing repo-wide);
   2. it calls `sqlite3.connect`;
   3. it executes NO write SQL — determined by AST, by inspecting the string
      literal passed to `.execute` / `.executemany` / `.executescript` and
      testing its leading keyword.

Condition 3 is what keeps this honest. A keyword scan of the whole file reports
`UPDATE` and `DROP` from prose in comments and docstrings — the first draft of

nobody answered (`/batch-done`).

import json
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

DISPOSITIONS = ("retried", "parked", "waived")


class Refused(Exception):

    """The bare stem of `given`, else of `scratchpad/CURRENT`; refused when neither names a folder."""

    if not stem:

        stem = dbcore.session_stem(cur.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()) if cur.is_file() else None
    if not stem or "/" in stem:

    refusals, dispositions, bad = [], [], []
    if not path.is_file():

    for n, raw in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):

    ts_held = [r.get("ts") for _, r in refusals]
    for n, d in dispositions:
        if d.get("refusal_ts") not in ts_held:
            problems.append(f"line {n}: a disposition for {d.get('refusal_ts')!r}, which no refusal of this file carries")
        elif d["refusal_ts"] in by_ts:
            problems.append(f"line {n}: {d['refusal_ts']!r} is disposed a second time")
        else:
            by_ts[d["refusal_ts"]] = d
    undisposed = 0
    if not refusals:
        print(f"no refusal captured for {stem}")
    for _, r in refusals:
        d = by_ts.get(r.get("ts"))
        if d is None:
            undisposed += 1
            state = "UNDISPOSED"
        else:
            state = f"{d['as']}" + (f" {d['gap_id']}" if d.get("gap_id") else "") + (f" ({_one_line(d['reason'], 80)})" if d.get("reason") else "")
        print(f"{r.get('ts')}  {r.get('verb')}  {_one_line(r.get('sentence'), 160)}  -> {state}")

    """The database the refusal names (`db`: a repository-relative or absolute path, `~` forms are not
    resolvable), else the one this process opens (GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, else the canonical file)."""

    for p in cand + [dbcore.db_path()]:

    if len(held) > 1:
        raise Refused(f"ts {args.ts!r} is carried by {len(held)} refusal lines, so it cannot name one: edit the file by hand")
    if any(d.get("refusal_ts") == args.ts for _, d in dispositions):

    reason = (args.reason or "").strip()

            raise Refused(f"{db} cannot answer for gap {args.gap_id!r}: {exc}")
        finally:
            con.close()
        if row is None:
            raise Refused(f"gap {args.gap_id!r} is not in the gaps table of {db}: parking needs a gap that holds the content")
        if not str(row[0]).startswith("OPEN"):
            raise Refused(f"gap {args.gap_id!r} is {row[0]!r}, not open: a closed gap holds nothing back")
    elif args.gap_id:
        raise Refused(f"--gap-id belongs to parked, not {args.disposition}")

        raise Refused("waived needs --reason: a refusal set aside without a reason is a refusal lost")
    line = {"kind": "disposition", "refusal_ts": args.ts, "as": args.disposition, "gap_id": args.gap_id or None,

    with open(dbcore.REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad" / stem / "refusals.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"disposed {args.ts} as {args.disposition}" + (f" {args.gap_id}" if args.gap_id else ""))
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("list", help="each refusal of a session and its disposition; exit 1 if any is undisposed")
    p.add_argument("--session", help="default: scratchpad/CURRENT")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_list)
    p = sub.add_parser("dispose", help="record what became of one refusal")
    p.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--ts", required=True, help="the refusal's ts, as `list` prints it")
    p.add_argument("--as", dest="disposition", required=True, choices=DISPOSITIONS)
    p.add_argument("--gap-id", help="parked: the open gap that holds the content")
    p.add_argument("--reason", help="waived: why; any other: optional")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    args.fn = cmd_dispose if args.cmd == "dispose" else cmd_list
    try:
        return args.fn(args)
    except Refused as exc:
        print(f"REFUSING: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# T088-BEGIN
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Section T088: a writer's refusal is kept, and every refusal a batch met is disposed")
# T-088. What a writer refused is the only record of what the batch held and could not write; it was printed once and lost.
# The capture is `dbcore.record_refusal` (one home, called by every place a writer says no); the disposition is
# `scripts/audit/refusal_register.py`. Everything here runs on a TEMPORARY tree that holds its own `scratchpad/CURRENT` and
# session folder (`dbcore.REPO_ROOT` is pointed at it for the call and restored), so no case reaches the real session's record.
import runpy  # noqa: E402

S88 = "session_t088-fixture"
_TS88 = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{6}$")
HAS88 = hasattr(dbcore, "record_refusal")
REG88 = None
try:
    import importlib.util as _ilu
    _spec88 = _ilu.spec_from_file_location("refusal_register", REPO / "scripts" / "audit" / "refusal_register.py")
    REG88 = _ilu.module_from_spec(_spec88)
    _spec88.loader.exec_module(REG88)
except Exception as _exc88:   # noqa: BLE001
    REG88_ERR = f"{type(_exc88).__name__}: {_exc88}"
else:
    REG88_ERR = None


@contextlib.contextmanager
def root88(current=S88, folder=S88):
    """A temporary tree with `scratchpad/CURRENT` (omitted when `current` is None) and a session folder (omitted when
    `folder` is None); `dbcore.REPO_ROOT` points at it inside the block."""
    base = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="t088-", dir=TMP))
    (base / "scratchpad").mkdir()
    if current is not None:
        (base / "scratchpad" / "CURRENT").write_text(current + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if folder:
        (base / "scratchpad" / folder).mkdir()
    old, dbcore.REPO_ROOT = dbcore.REPO_ROOT, base
    try:
        yield base
    finally:
        dbcore.REPO_ROOT = old


def file88(base, stem=S88):
    return base / "scratchpad" / stem / "refusals.jsonl"


def lines88(base, stem=S88):
    f = file88(base, stem)
    return [json.loads(x) for x in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()] if f.exists() else []


def refuse88(argv, sentence="a refusal; Nothing was written.", script="scripts/db.py"):
    """What a caller does at a catch point; returns whatever `record_refusal` returns (it must not raise)."""
    return dbcore.record_refusal(script, argv, sentence)


def run88(script, *argv):
    """Run `script`'s `__main__` in this process: (exit code or message, stdout, stderr). `dbcore.REPO_ROOT` is whatever the
    caller's `root88` set, so a refusal it keeps lands in the temporary tree."""
    out, err, old, code = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO(), sys.argv, None
    sys.argv = [script, *argv]
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            runpy.run_path(str(REPO / script), run_name="__main__")
    except SystemExit as exc:
        code = exc.code
    finally:
        sys.argv = old
    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()


def reg88(*argv):
    """(exit code, stdout, stderr) of `refusal_register.main(argv)`."""
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
        try:
            rc = REG88.main(list(argv))
        except SystemExit as exc:
            rc = exc.code
    return rc, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()


_SUCH88 = "99999999"   # a parameter id no database holds: built by the width, not read from data (add-gap refuses it)
_ARGV88 = ["add-gap", "--category", "SW", "--priority", "P1", "--description", "x", "--session", S88, "--parameter", _SUCH88]

if feature("T088-01", "the capture exists", HAS88, "dbcore.record_refusal"):
    with root88() as b:
        refuse88(_ARGV88, "add-gap parameter_id: no such row. Nothing was written.")
        ls = lines88(b)
    record("T088-01", "a refusal whose argv carries the running session appends exactly one line with its seven fields, and the verb is the subcommand",
           len(ls) == 1 and set(ls[0]) == {"ts", "session", "script", "verb", "argv", "sentence", "db"} and _TS88.match(ls[0]["ts"])
           and ls[0]["session"] == S88 and ls[0]["script"] == "scripts/db.py" and ls[0]["verb"] == "add-gap"
           and ls[0]["argv"] == _ARGV88 and ls[0]["sentence"] == "add-gap parameter_id: no such row. Nothing was written."
           and ls[0]["db"] == DB, ls)
    with root88() as b:
        refuse88(["--db", "/tmp/some-scratch.db", "--session", S88, "--parameter-id", "3"], "the engine said no", "scripts/assess/assess_cell.py")
        ls = lines88(b)
    record("T088-01b", "the engine's refusal names its own script as the verb and the database its --db flag gave",
           len(ls) == 1 and ls[0]["verb"] == "assess_cell" and ls[0]["db"] == "/tmp/some-scratch.db", ls)

    # T088-02: not the running session -> nothing is written.
    cases = {"another session": (S88, S88, ["add-gap", "--session", "session_other"]),
             "no --session": (S88, S88, ["add-gap", "--category", "SW"]),
             "--session with no value": (S88, S88, ["add-gap", "--session"]),
             "CURRENT missing": (None, S88, ["add-gap", "--session", S88]),
             "CURRENT empty": ("", S88, ["add-gap", "--session", S88]),
             "the folder named differently from CURRENT": (S88, S88 + "-other", ["add-gap", "--session", S88]),
             "no session folder": (S88, None, ["add-gap", "--session", S88]),
             "CURRENT naming a path": ("../escape", None, ["add-gap", "--session", "../escape"])}
    wrote = []
    for label, (cur, folder, argv) in cases.items():
        with root88(cur, folder) as b:
            refuse88(argv)
            got = [str(p.relative_to(b)) for p in b.rglob("refusals.jsonl")] + [str(p) for p in b.parent.glob("escape*")]
            if got:
                wrote.append((label, got))
    record("T088-02", "a call under another session, with no --session, with CURRENT missing or empty, with the folder named differently from CURRENT, "
           "or with no folder appends nothing", not wrote, wrote)

    # T088-03: the spellings argparse accepts for the session are all the running session.
    spell = {"--session=": ["add-gap", f"--session={S88}"], ".md form": ["add-gap", "--session", S88 + ".md"],
             "prefix --ses": ["add-gap", "--ses", S88], "last value wins": ["add-gap", "--session", "session_other", "--session", S88]}
    missed = []
    for label, argv in spell.items():
        with root88() as b:
            refuse88(argv)
            if len(lines88(b)) != 1:
                missed.append(label)
    with root88(S88 + ".md") as b:
        refuse88(["add-gap", "--session", S88])
        if len(lines88(b)) != 1:
            missed.append("CURRENT holding the .md pointer form")
    record("T088-03", "`--session=S`, `--session S.md`, an argparse prefix, the last of two --session flags, and a CURRENT holding the .md form are all the running session",
           not missed, missed)

    # T088-04: never raises, whatever is wrong with the file.
    with root88() as b:
        file88(b).mkdir()      # a directory where the file goes: the append fails (a read-only mode would not, as root)
        try:
            r = refuse88(_ARGV88)
            err = None
        except Exception as exc:   # noqa: BLE001
            r, err = None, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    record("T088-04", "a write that fails leaves the refusal's caller untouched (record_refusal returns, never raises)", err is None and r is None, err)

    # T088-05: privacy. The file is committed to a public repository.
    with root88() as b:
        refuse88(["add-source", "--session", S88, "--token", "SEKRIT-ONE", "--api-key=SEKRIT-TWO", "--Password", "SEKRIT-THREE",
                  "--db", "/home/alice/work/scratch.db", "--note", f"{b}/data/x.pdf and /Users/bob/y"],
                 f"{b}/data/x.pdf is not held; saw /home/alice/z and /root/w")
        raw = file88(b).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        ln = json.loads(raw)
    record("T088-05", "a secret-flag value, a home directory, and this repository's root are not stored (root relative, home as ~)",
           not any(w in raw for w in ("SEKRIT", "alice", "bob", "/root", str(b))) and ln["argv"][3:5] == ["--token", "<redacted>"]
           and "--api-key=<redacted>" in ln["argv"] and ln["argv"][ln["argv"].index("--Password") + 1] == "<redacted>"
           and ln["db"] == "~/work/scratch.db" and ln["sentence"] == "data/x.pdf is not held; saw ~/z and ~/w", raw)
    # nothing in db.py's own flags is named like a secret, so the redaction never eats a real value
    _flags = set(re.findall(r'add_argument\(\s*"(--[a-z0-9-]+)"', (REPO / "scripts" / "db.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    record("T088-05b", "no flag of db.py is named like a token, secret, password, credential or api key (the redaction would hide its value from the record)",
           bool(_flags) and not [f for f in _flags if dbcore._SECRET_FLAG.search(f)], sorted(f for f in _flags if dbcore._SECRET_FLAG.search(f)))

    # T088-06: two refusals of one retry loop are two lines with two keys.
    with root88() as b:
        for _ in range(3):
            refuse88(_ARGV88)
        tss = [x["ts"] for x in lines88(b)]
    record("T088-06", "refusals repeated at once (one retry loop) carry distinct ts, so a disposition names one", len(tss) == 3 and len(set(tss)) == 3, tss)

# T088-07..: the CLI. Every place a writer says no keeps its sentence, and none of them changes its exit or its words.
if feature("T088-07", "the capture exists", HAS88, "dbcore.record_refusal"):
    real = REPO / "scratchpad" / (REPO / "scratchpad" / "CURRENT").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() / "refusals.jsonl"
    size_before = real.stat().st_size if real.exists() else None
    r = cli("add-gap", "--category", "SW", "--priority", "P1", "--description", "x", "--session", "session_fixture", "--parameter", _SUCH88)
    size_after = real.stat().st_size if real.exists() else None
    record("T088-07", "db.py refusing under another session exits 1 with the same REFUSING: sentence, and the real session's refusals.jsonl does not change",
           r.returncode == 1 and r.stderr.startswith("REFUSING: add-gap parameter_id: gaps.parameter_id=") and r.stderr.rstrip().endswith("Nothing was written.")
           and size_before == size_after, (r.returncode, r.stderr[:160], size_before, size_after))

    eng = ["scripts/assess/assess_cell.py"]
    sites = {
        "db.py: a Refusal": (["scripts/db.py", "add-gap", "--category", "SW", "--priority", "P1", "--description", "x", "--session", S88, "--parameter", _SUCH88],
                             lambda c, o, e: isinstance(c, str) and c.startswith("REFUSING: add-gap parameter_id:"), "add-gap"),
        "db.py: a JSON error": (["scripts/db.py", "add-supersession-check", "--slug", "s", "--local-ref", "x", "--ref", "REF-00001", "--tier", "1",

                                 "--session", S88],
                                lambda c, o, e: c == 2 and json.loads(o)["error"].startswith("--search-strategy is not valid JSON"), "add-supersession-check"),
        "engine: the canonical-DB guard": (eng + ["--db", "data/guidebook.db", "--emit-sql", f"{TMP}/x.sql", "--parameter-id", "1", "--slug", "s", "--session", S88,
                                                  "--stamp", "2026-01-01 00:00"],
                                           lambda c, o, e: c == 1 and e == "REFUSING: this engine never writes the canonical DB (owner-gated).\n", "assess_cell"),
        "engine: a foreign --stamp": (eng + ["--db", DB, "--emit-sql", f"{TMP}/x.sql", "--parameter-id", "1", "--slug", "s", "--session", S88, "--stamp", "bad"],
                                      lambda c, o, e: c == 2 and e.startswith("REFUSING: --stamp 'bad' is not 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'") and e.endswith("Nothing was written.\n"), "assess_cell"),
        "engine: a Refusal": (eng + ["--db", DB, "--emit-sql", f"{TMP}/x.sql", "--parameter-id", _SUCH88, "--slug", "s", "--session", S88, "--stamp", "2026-01-01 00:00"],
                              lambda c, o, e: c == 1 and e.startswith(f"REFUSING: parameter_id {_SUCH88}: no such parameter."), "assess_cell"),
        "full_text.py: a REFUSING print": (["scripts/research/full_text.py", "--ref-id", "REF-99999", "--session", S88],
                                           lambda c, o, e: c == 2 and e == "REFUSING: REF-99999 is not an admitted source.\n", "full_text"),
    }
    bad, kept = [], {}
    for label, (argv, expect, verb) in sites.items():
        with root88() as b:
            code, out, err = run88(*argv)
            ls = lines88(b)
        if not expect(code, out, err):
            bad.append((label, "exit/words changed", code, out[:120], err[:160]))
        elif len(ls) != 1 or ls[0]["verb"] != verb or ls[0]["sentence"] not in (str(code) if isinstance(code, str) else "") + out + err:
            bad.append((label, "kept line wrong", ls))
        kept[label] = ls[0]["sentence"][:50] if ls else None
    record("T088-08", "each place a writer says no (db.py's Refusal and its JSON errors, the engine's four, full_text.py's REFUSING) exits as before, in the same words, "
           "and keeps exactly the sentence it said", not bad, bad)

    uncaptured = []

- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-088 merged (it writes `scratchpad/<session>/refusals.jsonl` and creates `scripts/audit/refusal_register.py`, which this task extends). Check by running: `grep -n 'def record_refusal' scripts/dbcore.py && python3 scripts/audit/refusal_register.py list --help`.
- **Owner decisions:** none. Nothing here writes a row; the classes are derived (statement 4 asks for that) and the cues are derived from the repository.
- **Tests that must be red before you start:** `T089-01` (section 6): no reader across sessions exists.
- **Set-up.**

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8. **Do nothing:** fails statement 4 (no one reads twenty sessions' files to see a recurring class). **Convention:** a coordinator reading the files by hand is the curated list rule 8 forbids. **Reuse:** T-088's script and its file format; the state graph's derivation of verb to tables to stage (`workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py`, class `Tree`); the check registry; the skill's own headings; the `gaps` table for a parked refusal's category and status. **Smallest code:** two subcommands in the existing script, and one line in `/batch-done`.

1. **`refusal_register.py register`**: reads every committed `scratchpad/*/refusals.jsonl` (`git ls-files`; an uncommitted file of the running session is added when `--session` names it) and prints the register of instances, one line each: session, `ts`, verb, the argv joined, the sentence, the disposition (or `UNDISPOSED`) and the gap id, with the gap's live `category` and `status` read from `data/guidebook.db` (`--db` overrides). Ends with `EXAMINED: <instances> refusal(s) in <sessions> session(s)`.
2. **`refusal_register.py classes [--session S]`**, every field derived at read time, never stored:
   - **signature**: the sentence with quoted values (`'…'`, `"…"`, `` `…` ``), numbers, and identifiers (`REF-\d+`, `GAP-[\w-]+`, `TERM-\d+`, `session_\S+`) each replaced by a placeholder, and whitespace collapsed; one function, so every class is computed the same way.
   - **cited rule ids**: every match in the sentence of `R\d+[a-z]?`, `OR-\d+[a-z]?`, `OD-\d+`, `OT-\d+`, `D-\d{4}`, `T-\d{3}`, `E\d+`.
   - **tables and stage**: for a `scripts/db.py` verb, `Tree(repo).verbs[verb]['writes']` and `Tree.stage(table)` (one `Tree` per run); for the engine, the stage of `specifications`. A verb the builder does not know prints `?`, never a guess.
   - **the classes**: instances grouped by signature, and again by verb, by stage and by cited id; for each group the count, the sessions, first and last seen, the share undisposed, and the dispositions and gap categories met. Ranked by count, recurring signatures first, so the top of the output is the area to resolve (the writer, the skill sentence, the schema or the stage).
   - **the triage type** of a class is what its instances were disposed as and filed under: `retried` (a policy refusal that was right), `parked` with the gap's `category` (`SW` for a missing verb or field and for a tool defect, the description says which), `waived` with its reasons. No second vocabulary is added (T-088 section 4a).
   - **the cue**: for each stage a class touches, the registered checks to re-run, derived as those whose `basis` begins with `<stage>/`, and those whose `cmd` script's text names a table the refused verb writes (read the script file named in `cmd`; never a list); and the skill section to re-read, the `## N. <stage> —` heading of `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`. Printed as `CUE <stage>: re-run <check ids>; re-read "<heading>"`.
   With `--session S`, only that session's instances and their cues are printed, and the exit is 1 if any of them is undisposed.
   **Chosen (authoring 2026-11-13): import `Tree` from the state graph's builder.** Rejected: copying its `_derive_verbs` (a second home for the verb-to-table derivation, rule 8) and reading the generated `graph.json` (generated on a date and stale between builds: `python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('workplan/pipeline-state-graph/graph.json'))['generated'])"`). If the builder moves, this import is a caller to sweep (rule 4).
   **Chosen:** the cue is printed, not run. Rejected: running the checks from the reader (the gate already runs checks; a second runner is the duplicate CLAUDE.md §8 forbids, and §1 asks that suites be run rarely and on purpose).
3. **`/batch-done` reads the cue.** In `.claude/commands/batch-done.md`, replace T-088's `list` line by `python3 scripts/audit/refusal_register.py classes --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"` and add: "For each `CUE` line, run the named checks once and re-read the named skill section before calling the batch done; say in the pull request what each showed. A refusal in a batch is the sign that the stage it names may not have been performed as the skill says." Keep T-088's disposition sentence.

```

**Step 2: red before, green after** (cases `T089-01`… in `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py`; prefix free: `git grep -c 'T089-' scripts/tests/`). Fixtures: a temporary tree with two session folders, each holding a `refusals.jsonl` built by T-088's `dbcore.record_refusal` (never typed JSON), from refusals produced by real `db.py` calls on a scratch copy under each fixture session; one disposed `parked` with a gap built on the copy (`TASK-FIXTURE`), one `retried`, one undisposed.
- `T089-01` `register` lists every instance of both sessions with its disposition and gap category; red before (no subcommand: assert the exit and the `EXAMINED:` line, so an absent subcommand cannot pass).
- `T089-02` two refusals with the same sentence but different quoted values and ids fall in one signature class; two different sentences do not.
- `T089-03` the stage of an `add-extraction` refusal is the stage the state graph gives `source_value_extractions` (read from `Tree`, not typed); a verb unknown to the builder prints `?`.
- `T089-04` the cue for a judgment-stage refusal names every registered check whose `basis` begins with that stage (the set read from the registry in the test) and the skill heading for that stage.
- `T089-05` `classes --session <the fixture with an undisposed refusal>` exits 1; for the fully disposed one, 0.
- Seeded defect: make the signature keep numbers; `T089-02` goes red; restore.

**Step 3: after-run.** The same loop with `after-`; nothing new may fail.
## 9. Stop conditions

Stop and report when: T-088 is not merged, or its line shape differs from its section 4 item 1; a reader across sessions already exists; `Tree` cannot be imported from `scripts/audit/` without changing the builder (report what it needs; do not change the builder in this task); a check green before is red after; `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` changes.
